title: DNS
hook: You typed a name, not a number — something has to translate before your request can even leave.

steps.caption: Before anything else, your phone asks: what address does "example.com" actually point to?

nodeCaptions.dns: DNS is the internet's phone book — it maps names humans type to IP addresses machines route.

steps.caption: DNS looks it up and answers with the real address.

nodeCaptions.client: Now your device knows exactly where to send the actual request.

steps.caption: Only now does your real request go out — straight to that address.

nodeCaptions.server: The server never sees the name you typed — only the IP address DNS resolved it to.

takeaways: DNS turns a name you can remember into the IP address a router can actually use.
This lookup happens before your real request goes anywhere — it's an extra round trip, hidden from you.
The server itself only ever sees the resolved IP, never the domain name you typed.

quiz.question: What does DNS actually do?
choices: It encrypts your request so no one can read it
It translates a domain name into the IP address that name points to
It speeds up your internet connection
It stores a copy of every website
quiz.explanation: DNS is purely a lookup — name in, IP address out. It doesn't encrypt, cache the site's content, or affect your connection speed directly.
